models.model_label: Table 4 Easton et al. regression-based pre- and post-restatement cost-of-capital estimation
models.sample_description: 292 restatements from 1997–2001 for which analyst forecasts are available before and after the restatement. The table reports separate fits using the pre-restatement and post-restatement price and forecast inputs.
models.method_reported: Easton et al. (2002) regression-based estimation technique
models.method_details: The paper identifies this as a regression-based estimation technique, but does not name the underlying regression estimator. The regression coefficients are used to compute the estimated cost of equity capital (re) and growth in residual income (gri); the paper describes the fit as simultaneously estimating the cost of capital and growth.

dependent_variable.name: X_i,T / B_i,0 (four-year cum-dividend earnings scaled by current book value of equity per share)
dependent_variable.definition: X_i,T is aggregate four-year cum-dividend earnings: FY1 and FY2 are summed, the long-term growth rate is applied to estimate FY3 and FY4, and current dividends are included as expected dividends in periods 1–4 and reinvested at the estimated cost of capital. B_i,0 is the firm’s current book value of equity per share. FY1 and FY2 are one- and two-year-ahead analyst EPS forecasts; the long-term growth rate comes from I/B/E/S. The dependent variable is X_i,T divided by B_i,0.

evidence.quote: Xi;T equals aggregate four year cum-dividend earnings. This variable is computed by summing FY1 and FY2, and applying the long-term growth rate to estimate FY3 and FY4. Dividends are added to this summation by using current dividends as an expectation for dividends in periods one through four, and reinvesting the dividends at the estimated cost of capital.
Bi;0 represents the firm’s current book value of equity per share.
The mean one-year ahead forecast (FY1), mean two-year ahead forecast (FY2), and the long-term growth rate (LTG) are obtained from I/B/E/S.

To deal with issues of IBES long term growth rates being poor proxies for investors’ long term growth expectations, we utilize Easton et al.’s (2002) regressionbased estimation technique that simultaneously estimates the cost of capital and the expected growth in residual income.

preprocessing.description: The authors require observations to have the inputs for all cost-of-capital estimation models so the same observations are used for pre/post changes across models. They exclude observations missing FY2 or long-term-growth forecasts, with negative FY2 forecasts, without analyst coverage after the restatement, or after delisting.

evidence.quote: We require that a firm have available data for all of our estimation models, to ensure that we have the same observations when we compute changes in the cost of capital across different models. Thus, if the firm has a missing FY2 or long-term growth forecast, or has a negative FY2 forecast, they will not be included in our final sample. We also end up eliminating observations where analyst coverage is dropped subsequent to the restatement, or the firm is delisted.

scope.quote: Using Easton et al. (2002) simultaneous estimation of growth and the cost of capital, we estimate a relative percentage increase in the estimated cost of capital of 7.65%.

review_notes: Principal question: how accounting restatements change the firm’s cost of capital and expected future cash flows. The source’s main event-study family tests pre/post cost-of-capital changes (Tables 3–5). Table 4 is retained because the authors use its actual regression-based Easton et al. estimator within that primary question to infer aggregate cost-of-capital and growth changes. Table 3 and Table 5 are mean, sign, and signed-rank tests rather than regressions. Table 6 is described as a cross-sectional analysis of factors associated with larger revisions and is secondary to the principal pre/post cost-of-capital test; its Models 1–3 are excluded. The previous Table 6 Models 2 and 3 selection is replaced by the source-selected Table 4 fitted regression.
results_review_notes: The frozen target is Table 4’s separate pre-restatement and post-restatement regression fits; no other tables, estimator families or robustness horizons are added.

Gamma0 and gamma1 coefficients and their explicitly labelled standard errors match the selected Table 4 cells. Table-level R-squared is retained as an auxiliary fit summary; re and gri are transformed outputs reported separately from coefficient inference.

The source reports no author t/z statistic or p-value for the Table 4 coefficients. The conventional zero-null Wald ratios are helper-derived from printed coefficients and genuine sampling standard errors, with reference, tail and degrees of freedom left unknown.
The 7.65% change is a reported pre/post summary attached as an auxiliary row to the existing post-fit result set; no significance test for that comparison is reported.

Table 2 reports FY1, FY2 and LTG input summaries for a reduced 286-restatement sample; they are captured as components of the retained dependent variable. Table 2 reports no exact distribution of X_i,T/B_i,0 or P_i,0/B_i,0. Its separate re_gls, re_gm and re_pfe rows belong to other cost-of-capital estimators and are outside the selected baseline model.
The Table 2 FY2 variable definition repeats the one-year-ahead description; this source wording is preserved.
